prompts.L1:

A signaling apparatus for command and/or indicating devices includes a base unit having at least two light sources which each generate light and are arranged on the base unit at a spacing from one another, and at least two light modules which are stacked along a main axis of the signaling apparatus and are operatively connected to the light sources such that light generated by the light sources is coupled into the light modules in a beam direction parallel to the main axis, the light modules each having a reflection region for reflecting at least in part the light coupled into the light modules in a signaling direction. A particular reflection region occupies only a portion of the light module in a peripheral direction of the corresponding light module perpendicular to the main axis of the signaling apparatus, which portion is smaller than a total periphery of the light module.

outputs.L1: A signaling apparatus for command and/or indicating devices includes a base unit having at least two light sources, each configured to generate light and arranged on the base unit at a distance from one another, and at least two light modules stacked along a main axis of the signaling apparatus. The light modules are operatively connected to the light sources such that light generated by the light sources is coupled into the light modules in a beam direction parallel to the main axis. Each light module includes a reflection region configured to reflect, at least in part, the light coupled into the light module in a signaling direction. A respective reflection region occupies only a portion of the light module in a peripheral direction of the corresponding light module perpendicular to the main axis of the signaling apparatus, the portion being smaller than the total periphery of the light module.
outputs.L2: A signaling device for control and/or display equipment comprises a base element with at least two spaced-apart light emitters, each configured to produce light. The device also includes at least two illumination modules arranged one above the other along a principal axis of the signaling device. These modules are functionally linked to the light emitters so that the light produced by the emitters enters the modules in a beam path running parallel to the principal axis. Each illumination module includes a reflective section that redirects at least part of the incoming light into a signaling direction. Each reflective section extends over only part of the circumference of its respective illumination module, measured in a peripheral direction perpendicular to the principal axis, and this part is less than the full outer perimeter of the module.
outputs.L3:
The signaling apparatus is designed for use with command and/or indicating devices, particularly in applications where visual signals must be generated in a clear and reliable manner.

The apparatus comprises a base unit that includes at least two light sources arranged at a distance from one another. These light sources are positioned so that they can emit light into the signaling structure of the apparatus. Along a main axis of the signaling apparatus, at least two light modules are arranged in a stacked configuration. This modular arrangement allows multiple optical signaling elements to be combined in a compact structure.

Light emitted by the light sources is coupled into the respective light modules in a beam direction that extends parallel to the main axis of the signaling apparatus. In this way, the light can be guided efficiently from the base unit into the stacked modules.

Each light module includes a reflection region configured to redirect the incoming light. The reflection region reflects the light in a signaling direction, so that the light becomes visible from outside the apparatus as a signal. The reflection region is formed only over a portion of the peripheral region of the corresponding light module, rather than extending around the entire circumference. This partial peripheral arrangement enables targeted light emission and can allow different light modules or light sources to generate distinct visual signals in defined directions.
outputs.L4:
A signaling apparatus for command and/or indicating devices comprises a base unit and one or more light modules arranged in a stack along a main axis of the apparatus. The base unit contains a plurality of light sources, such as LEDs, which are spaced apart from one another around the main axis. These light sources are configured to emit light into the stacked light modules, so that each module can receive light from one or more associated light sources.

Each light module extends at least partially around the main axis and is designed to guide light within the module. Instead of emitting light uniformly over its entire circumference, the module includes at least one partial peripheral reflection region. This reflection region is arranged only over a selected circumferential portion of the module and is shaped or positioned to redirect light outward in a defined signaling direction. As a result, light can be emitted from only a desired sector of the module, while other circumferential regions remain unilluminated or emit little to no light.

The apparatus therefore permits selective and directional signaling. By activating particular light sources in the base unit, light can be coupled into corresponding portions of one or more stacked light modules. The partial reflection regions then deflect the light toward predetermined viewing directions. This makes it possible to generate different visual signals, such as status indications, warnings, position-dependent signals, or directional indicators, without requiring the entire circumference of each module to be illuminated.

The stacked construction allows multiple signaling levels to be provided along the main axis of the device. Each light module may be assigned a specific function, color, or signaling direction. For example, different modules may indicate different operating states, or a single module may emit light only toward a machine operator, a service side, or another defined observation region. The use of spaced light sources in the base unit also simplifies the electrical arrangement, since the active light-generating components can be concentrated in the base unit while the stacked modules primarily serve to guide and redirect the light.

In this way, the signaling apparatus provides a compact, modular, and flexible solution for command and/or indicating devices. It enables targeted light output from selected peripheral portions of a module rather than omnidirectional illumination around the full circumference, thereby improving signal clarity, reducing unwanted light emission, and allowing different signaling zones to be realized within a single stacked device.
outputs.L5:
A signaling apparatus is a device or system designed to transmit information, warnings, or instructions through visual, audible, electronic, or mechanical signals. It plays an important role in many environments, including transportation, industrial facilities, public safety systems, communication networks, and emergency response operations.

In transportation, a signaling apparatus may include traffic lights, railway signals, warning beacons, or maritime navigation lights. These systems help control movement, prevent accidents, and ensure that operators and pedestrians receive clear instructions. For example, railway signaling equipment informs train operators when to stop, slow down, or proceed, improving safety across busy rail networks.

In industrial settings, a signaling apparatus is often used to alert workers to changes in machine status, hazards, or emergency conditions. Sirens, flashing lights, control panel indicators, and automated alarm systems can warn personnel about equipment failures, fire risks, gas leaks, or restricted areas. By providing quick and noticeable alerts, these devices help reduce response time and protect both people and property.

Modern signaling apparatuses are often integrated with digital control systems. Sensors, programmable controllers, wireless communication modules, and monitoring software allow signals to be triggered automatically based on real-time data. This makes signaling systems more reliable, efficient, and adaptable to complex operational needs.

Overall, a signaling apparatus is essential wherever information must be communicated quickly and clearly. Whether used for safety, coordination, navigation, or operational control, it helps people and systems respond appropriately to changing conditions.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for a signaling apparatus for command/indicating devices with a base unit, spaced light sources, stacked light modules, axial light coupling, and partial peripheral reflection regions.
counterfactuals.output: A signaling apparatus for command and/or indicating devices includes a base unit and a plurality of light modules stackable on the base unit along an axial direction. The base unit carries a plurality of mutually spaced light sources, each assigned to a respective light channel. Each light module includes an axially extending light coupling region for receiving light from an associated light source or from an adjacent module and for guiding the light through the stack. At least one light module includes one or more peripheral reflection regions extending only over a partial circumferential region of the module, the reflection regions being configured to deflect axially coupled light radially outward for visible indication while permitting further axial light transmission to another stacked light module. The arrangement enables multiple separately controllable optical indications in a compact modular stack, with simplified electrical connection through the base unit and optical distribution between modules.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a formal technical description in patent language for an optical signaling device comprising a base with at least two separated light sources and stacked light modules that reflect light sideways.
counterfactuals.output:
An optical signaling device is provided comprising a base assembly and a plurality of light-transmitting signaling modules arranged in a stacked configuration. The base assembly includes at least two mutually spaced light sources disposed at separated positions within or on the base assembly. The light sources may comprise light emitting diodes, laser diodes, incandescent lamps, or other electrically energizable optical emitters, and are arranged to emit light generally upwardly toward respective light receiving regions of the stacked modules.

Each signaling module comprises a light-transmissive body defining a lower light input region, an upper region, and a peripheral side wall. The modules are arranged one above another along a stacking axis, such that light emitted by the separated light sources enters the stacked modules from the base assembly. At least one of the modules includes an optical reflecting surface positioned and configured to intercept light entering the module and to redirect at least a portion of the intercepted light laterally through the peripheral side wall. The reflecting surface may be inclined relative to the stacking axis and may be formed as an internal reflective face, a prism surface, a mirrored surface, a total-internal-reflection surface, a faceted reflector, or a diffusive reflective structure.

The at least two separated light sources are optically associated with different light paths in the stacked module arrangement. In one embodiment, each light source is aligned with a corresponding optical channel, window, lens, or light guide portion extending through one or more of the modules. Each module may include a respective reflecting portion located in optical communication with one of the light sources, whereby energization of a selected light source causes light to be directed into a corresponding module and reflected sideways to provide a visible signaling output from that module. The separated arrangement of the light sources permits independent illumination of different portions of the stack, different angular sectors, different colors, or different signal levels.

In certain embodiments, the modules are substantially annular or cylindrical and are stacked coaxially on the base assembly. Each module may comprise a transparent or translucent lens element having one or more internal oblique surfaces for redirecting light radially outwardly. The reflecting surfaces of adjacent modules may be positioned at different heights relative to the base assembly so that light from the respective light sources is directed laterally outward at different vertical levels. The modules may further include optical isolation structures, opaque partitions, spacing collars, or light-blocking interfaces to reduce optical cross-talk between adjacent modules or between light paths associated with different light sources.

The base assembly may include electrical conductors, a controller, switching circuitry, a power interface, and mounting features for securing the signaling device to a support surface. The controller may be configured to selectively energize the at least two separated light sources individually or in combination to generate predetermined signaling patterns. The signaling patterns may include steady illumination, flashing illumination, sequential illumination, color-coded indication, or directional indication.

According to one aspect, the optical signaling device comprises: a base; a first light source and a second light source mounted to the base and spaced apart from one another; a first light module supported above the base and having a first reflecting surface arranged to receive light from the first light source and reflect the received light laterally outwardly; and a second light module stacked with the first light module and having a second reflecting surface arranged to receive light from the second light source and reflect the received light laterally outwardly. The first and second reflecting surfaces are disposed at different elevations in the stacked arrangement, thereby producing laterally emitted optical signals from different module levels.

According to another aspect, the stacked light modules are configured such that light emitted by one of the separated light sources passes through at least a portion of a lower module before reaching a reflecting surface of an upper module. The reflecting surface of the upper module redirects the light sideways through an outer wall of the upper module, while another light source is associated with a lower reflecting surface for producing a separate lateral light output from a lower module. In this manner, a compact stacked optical signaling device is formed in which multiple signaling outputs are generated from a plurality of vertically arranged modules using spatially separated light sources positioned in a common base.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Create an abstract for an invention involving modular signal lamps: light sources arranged in a base, beam direction parallel to the apparatus axis, and reflection regions in each module that cover less than the full periphery.
counterfactuals.output: A modular signal lamp apparatus includes a base defining an apparatus axis and a plurality of lamp modules mountable to the base. Each module includes at least one light source arranged so that a principal beam direction is substantially parallel to the apparatus axis. The modules further include optical reflection regions configured to redirect light emitted by the light sources outwardly from the apparatus. In each module, the reflection region extends over only a portion of the module periphery, less than a full circumferential surround, thereby enabling selective angular light emission and modular configuration of signaling directions. Multiple modules may be stacked, exchanged, or angularly oriented relative to the base to provide desired signal visibility patterns while maintaining a compact axial light-source arrangement.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Rephrase the following invention concept as a patent abstract: a command/indicating signaling apparatus has stacked modules, base-mounted light sources coupled axially into the modules, and partial circumferential reflectors that redirect light outward.
counterfactuals.output: A command and/or indicating signaling apparatus includes a plurality of axially stacked signaling modules mounted on a base. One or more light sources are arranged in the base and optically coupled to the stacked modules so as to emit light generally along an axial direction into the modules. Each module includes at least one partial circumferential reflector configured to intercept the axially transmitted light and redirect the light radially outward through a circumferential portion of the module. The reflector arrangement enables selective outward light emission from individual stacked modules while allowing the light sources to remain commonly located in the base, thereby simplifying assembly, reducing wiring, and improving modularity of the signaling apparatus.
